Colorectal Cancer Risk & Survival — Exploratory Data Analysis¶

Project Overview

This project performs an exploratory data analysis of a colorectal cancer patient dataset.

The analysis focuses on understanding patterns and relationships among:

  • Demographic characteristics
  • Lifestyle and dietary factors
  • Family and previous cancer history
  • Cancer stage and tumor aggressiveness
  • Screening and healthcare access
  • Treatment-related factors
  • Survival status
  • Recurrence patterns

The goal is to generate meaningful, data-driven insights from the dataset rather than build a machine learning prediction model.

1. Project Objectives

The main objectives of this analysis are to:

  1. Understand the structure and characteristics of the dataset.
  2. Assess data quality, including missing values and duplicate records.
  3. Explore demographic and clinical characteristics of patients.
  4. Analyze lifestyle and potential risk-related factors.
  5. Examine survival patterns across different patient groups.
  6. Investigate the relationship between cancer stage, tumor aggressiveness, treatment, and survival.
  7. Analyze recurrence patterns among patients.
  8. Identify important patterns and relationships using statistical summaries and visualizations.
  9. Present actionable insights and conclusions from the analysis.

Note: This is an exploratory and descriptive data analysis project. Observed relationships should not be interpreted as causal or as medical advice.

2. Dataset Overview

The dataset contains patient-level records related to colorectal cancer.

Main categories of variables

Demographic Variables

  • Age
  • Gender
  • Race
  • Region
  • Urban/Rural status
  • Socioeconomic status

Risk and Lifestyle Variables

  • Family history
  • Previous cancer history
  • Diet type
  • BMI
  • Physical activity
  • Smoking
  • Alcohol consumption
  • Red meat consumption
  • Fiber consumption

Clinical Variables

  • Stage at diagnosis
  • Tumor aggressiveness
  • Time to diagnosis

Healthcare and Treatment Variables

  • Colonoscopy access
  • Screening regularity
  • Insurance coverage
  • Treatment access
  • Chemotherapy
  • Radiotherapy
  • Surgery
  • Follow-up adherence

Outcome Variables

  • Survival status
  • Recurrence
  • Time to recurrence

Analysis Workflow¶

Dataset → Data Quality → Exploratory Analysis → Demographic Analysis → Clinical Analysis → Lifestyle Analysis → Healthcare & Treatment Analysis → Recurrence Analysis → Correlation Analysis → Key Findings → Conclusion

This notebook is focused on descriptive and exploratory data analysis. No machine-learning prediction model is used.

5.Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

Exploratory Data Analysis is performed to understand the distribution, composition, and relationships within the patient dataset.

Data Quality Assessment

Before performing exploratory analysis, the dataset is checked for:

  • Missing values
  • Duplicate records
  • Duplicate patient IDs
  • Incorrect or unexpected data types
  • Basic numerical summaries
  • Categorical value distributions
In [4]:
# Check for missing values

missing_values = df.isnull().sum()

missing_summary = pd.DataFrame({
    "Missing Values": missing_values,
    "Missing Percentage": (missing_values / len(df) * 100).round(2)
})

display(missing_summary)

print("Total missing values:", df.isnull().sum().sum())

# Check for duplicate records and duplicate patient IDs

duplicate_rows = df.duplicated().sum()
duplicate_patient_ids = df["Patient_ID"].duplicated().sum()

print("Duplicate rows:", duplicate_rows)
print("Duplicate Patient IDs:", duplicate_patient_ids)

if duplicate_rows == 0 and duplicate_patient_ids == 0:
    print("\nData quality check: No duplicate records or duplicate patient IDs found.")


# Categorical variable summary

})

display(categorical_summary)

6. Data Preparation for Analysis

The dataset does not require machine-learning preprocessing because this project focuses on exploratory and descriptive analysis.

The Patient_ID column is an identifier and will not be used for statistical comparisons or visualizations.

No train-test split, feature encoding, normalization, or model-specific preprocessing is required.

8. Demographic Analysis

This section examines whether survival patterns differ across demographic groups.

The analysis focuses on:

  • Gender
  • Race
  • Region
  • Urban/Rural residence
  • Socioeconomic status
  • Age groups
In [8]:
# Create age groups for comparative analysis

analysis_df["Age_Group"] = pd.cut(
    analysis_df["Age"],
    bins=[0, 29, 39, 49, 59, 69, 79, 100],
    labels=[
        "<30",
        "30-39",
        "40-49",
        "50-59",
        "60-69",
        "70-79",
        "80+"
    ]
)

display(analysis_df["Age_Group"].value_counts().sort_index())

# Helper function for survival-rate analysis

def survival_rate_table(data, column):
    table = pd.crosstab(
        data[column],
        data["Survival_Status"],
        normalize="index"
    ) * 100
    
    return table.round(2)


def plot_survival_rate(data, column, title, order=None, figsize=(10, 5)):
    survival = (
        data.groupby(column)["Survival_Status"]
        .apply(lambda x: (x == "Survived").mean() * 100)
        .reset_index(name="Survival_Rate")
    )
    
    if order is not None:
        survival[column] = pd.Categorical(
            survival[column],
            categories=order,
            ordered=True
        )
        survival = survival.sort_values(column)
    
    plt.figure(figsize=figsize)
    
    sns.barplot(
        data=survival,
        x=column,
        y="Survival_Rate"
    )
    
    plt.title(title)
    plt.xlabel(column.replace("_", " "))
    plt.ylabel("Survival Rate (%)")
    plt.xticks(rotation=30)
    plt.ylim(0, 100)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    
    return survival

# Survival by Gender

display(survival_rate_table(analysis_df, "Gender"))

plot_survival_rate(
    analysis_df,
    "Gender",
    "Survival Rate by Gender"
)

# Survival by Age Group

display(survival_rate_table(analysis_df, "Age_Group"))

plot_survival_rate(
    analysis_df,
    "Age_Group",
    "Survival Rate by Age Group",

)

11. Healthcare Access and Treatment Analysis

This section investigates how healthcare access and treatment-related variables are associated with survival.

Variables include:

  • Colonoscopy access
  • Screening regularity
  • Insurance coverage
  • Treatment access
  • Chemotherapy
  • Radiotherapy
  • Surgery
  • Follow-up adherence

These comparisons show associations in the dataset and should not be interpreted as evidence that a particular treatment directly causes better or worse survival.

In [11]:
# Healthcare access variables

healthcare_columns = [
    "Colonoscopy_Access",
    "Screening_Regularity",
    "Insurance_Coverage",
    "Treatment_Access",
    "Chemotherapy_Received",
    "Radiotherapy_Received",
    "Surgery_Received",
    "Follow_Up_Adherence"
]

for column in healthcare_columns:
    print(f"\n{'=' * 60}")
    print(column)
    print("=" * 60)

plot_survival_rate(

)
# Survival by treatment access

    "Treatment_Access",

)
# Compare survival across treatment types

treatment_columns = [
    "Chemotherapy_Received",
    "Radiotherapy_Received",
    "Surgery_Received"
]

treatment_results = []

for column in treatment_columns:
    temp = (
        analysis_df.groupby(column)["Survival_Status"]
        .apply(lambda x: (x == "Survived").mean() * 100)
        .reset_index(name="Survival_Rate")
    )
    
    temp["Treatment"] = column.replace("_Received", "")
    temp = temp.rename(columns={column: "Received"})
    
    treatment_results.append(temp)

treatment_survival = pd.concat(
    treatment_results,
    ignore_index=True
)

display(treatment_survival)

)

12. Recurrence Analysis

Recurrence is analyzed separately because Time_to_Recurrence is most meaningful for patients who experienced recurrence.

The analysis will examine:

  • Overall recurrence rate
  • Time to recurrence
  • Recurrence by cancer stage
  • Recurrence by tumor aggressiveness
  • Recurrence by survival status
In [12]:
# Recurrence rate

recurrence_rate = (
    analysis_df["Recurrence"]
    .value_counts(normalize=True)
    .mul(100)
    .round(2)
)

display(recurrence_rate)

print(
    f"Overall recurrence rate: "
    f"{(analysis_df['Recurrence'] == 'Yes').mean() * 100:.2f}%"
)
# Time to recurrence among patients with recurrence

recurrence_df = analysis_df[
    analysis_df["Recurrence"] == "Yes"
].copy()

print(
    "Number of patients with recurrence:",
    len(recurrence_df)
)

display(
    recurrence_df["Time_to_Recurrence"]
    .describe()
)

# Distribution of time to recurrence

sns.histplot(
    data=recurrence_df,

)

13. Correlation Analysis

Correlation analysis is performed for numerical variables only.

The numerical variables in this dataset include:

  • Age
  • BMI
  • Time to Recurrence

Because categorical variables represent groups rather than continuous numerical measurements, they are not included in the standard Pearson correlation heatmap.

15. Key Findings

The following section summarizes the major patterns identified during the exploratory analysis.

When interpreting the results, the analysis focuses on associations observed in the dataset rather than causal relationships.

Key areas to evaluate include:

  • Which age groups show different survival patterns?
  • How does survival vary across cancer stages?
  • Is tumor aggressiveness associated with survival?
  • Which lifestyle variables show noticeable differences in survival rates?
  • How do screening and healthcare access relate to survival?
  • How does follow-up adherence relate to survival?
  • How does recurrence vary across cancer stages and tumor aggressiveness?
  • Which numerical variables show meaningful correlations?
In [15]:
# Generate a compact summary of important survival rates

summary_factors = [
    "Gender",
    "Age_Group",
    "Stage_at_Diagnosis",
    "Tumor_Aggressiveness",
    "Smoking_Status",
    "Physical_Activity_Level",
    "Screening_Regularity",
    "Treatment_Access",
    "Follow_Up_Adherence"
]

summary_results = []

for column in summary_factors:
    result = (
        analysis_df.groupby(column)["Survival_Status"]
        .apply(lambda x: (x == "Survived").mean() * 100)
        .reset_index(name="Survival_Rate")
    )
    
    result["Factor"] = column
    
    summary_results.append(result)

survival_summary = pd.concat(
    summary_results,
    ignore_index=True
)

survival_summary["Survival_Rate"] = (
    survival_summary["Survival_Rate"].round(2)
)

display(survival_summary)

16. Conclusion

This exploratory data analysis provided an overview of colorectal cancer patient characteristics and examined patterns associated with survival and recurrence.

The analysis covered demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, clinical characteristics, healthcare access, treatment-related variables, and recurrence.

The visualizations and comparative analyses help identify groups and variables that show noticeable differences in survival or recurrence within the dataset.

Important Interpretation

These findings represent associations observed in the available data. They should not be interpreted as proof of causation, medical recommendations, or individual patient predictions.

Project Outcome

The project demonstrates practical data analyst skills including:

  • Data loading and inspection
  • Data quality assessment
  • Missing-value analysis
  • Duplicate detection
  • Descriptive statistics
  • Data visualization
  • Group-wise analysis
  • Survival-rate analysis
  • Recurrence analysis
  • Correlation analysis
  • Insight generation

17. Final Takeaways

Data Quality

  • The dataset contains 89,945 patient records and 30 variables.
  • Missing values and duplicate records were assessed before analysis.
  • Patient ID was excluded from analytical comparisons because it is an identifier.

Exploratory Analysis

  • Demographic, lifestyle, clinical, healthcare, treatment, survival, and recurrence variables were explored.
  • Numerical distributions were examined using histograms and boxplots.
  • Categorical variables were analyzed using counts and survival-rate comparisons.

Clinical Insights

  • Cancer stage and tumor aggressiveness were examined in relation to survival.
  • Recurrence patterns were compared across cancer stages and tumor aggressiveness.

Healthcare Insights

  • Screening, healthcare access, treatment access, and follow-up adherence were compared with survival outcomes.

Analytical Limitation

The dataset is observational. Differences between groups may be influenced by multiple factors, so the results should be interpreted as descriptive associations rather than causal effects.
